column2: Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
column3: I mapped G-code Parser to Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it interprets and validates G-code commands before they are executed by the simulated firmware.
column4: Reuse Marlin/Klipper command semantics and build a custom HoneyPrint parser/validator. (Python (re + shlex + dict-based dispatcher))
column5: Parse incoming G-code/firmware commands, validate syntax/parameters, and identify the requested operation.
column6: Normalized validated command objects or believable firmware-style errors for invalid input.

column2: Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control; Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer
column3: I mapped Printer State to Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control and Stage 3 > Hardware > AM machine / 3D printer because the state machine tracks firmware-controlled values that represent the current physical condition of the emulated printer.
column4: Maintain a custom HoneyPrint printer state machine shared with the physical simulator. (Python (dataclasses + enum + asyncio))
column5: Track motion, thermal, extrusion, power, job, and fault state as commands and simulated physics evolve.
column6: One coherent printer-state representation used by firmware responses, telemetry, and downstream physical models.

column2: Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control; Stage 3 > Hardware > Printer controller (MCU / SoC)
column3: I mapped Command Executor to Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control and Stage 3 > Hardware > Printer controller (MCU / SoC) because it executes validated firmware commands and applies the resulting controller-level state changes.
column4: Build custom Marlin/Klipper execution adapters that update shared simulator state and return firmware-appropriate responses. (Python (asyncio + Adapter pattern + command handlers))
column5: Execute validated commands against the simulated printer and generate believable protocol-specific responses.
column6: State changes and Marlin/Klipper-style acknowledgements, status replies, or fault responses.

column2: Stage 3 > Hardware > Cameras, thermal & process sensors; Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics
column3: I mapped Sensor Emulation to Stage 3 > Hardware > Cameras, thermal & process sensors and Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics because it generates virtual sensor readings that are consumed as runtime monitoring data.
column4: Build/extend HoneyPrint sensor views coupled to the physical models. (Python (dataclasses + random + numpy))
column5: Expose believable thermistor, endstop, filament, and other sensor observations instead of perfect internal model values.
column6: Sensor readings and sensor/fault events consumed by firmware, telemetry, and analyst logging.

column2: Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
column3: I mapped Firmware Adapter to Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it translates Marlin and Klipper command dialects into a common internal firmware-control interface.
column4: Reuse Marlin/Klipper command semantics and maintain custom adapters over the shared simulator. (Python (asyncio + abc + Adapter pattern + re))
column5: Support multiple firmware dialects while keeping one coherent underlying printer state.
column6: Marlin- and Klipper-style commands translated into shared simulator actions and protocol-specific responses.

column2: Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
column3: I mapped Job Control to Stage 3 > Software > Build-execution software / HMI and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because start, pause, resume, and cancel operations are initiated through build controls and must also update firmware job state.
column4: Extend custom HoneyPrint job lifecycle handlers using OctoPrint/firmware-compatible semantics. (Python (asyncio + enum + dataclasses))
column5: Support print start, pause, resume, cancel, and job-state transitions through management and firmware paths.
column6: Consistent print-job lifecycle state propagated to commands, telemetry, and the physical simulator.

column2: Stage 2 > Hardware > Job-package storage; Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control
column3: I mapped Virtual SD to Stage 2 > Hardware > Job-package storage and Stage 3 > Software > Printer firmware & motion control because it stores printer-local G-code files and exposes them through firmware commands for selection and execution.
column4: Build/extend virtual SD behavior using persistent filesystem storage and firmware-style file semantics. (Python (pathlib + aiofiles + os + shutil))
column5: Expose realistic printer-local file listing, selection, persistence, and print-file behavior.
column6: Persistent G-code inventory that firmware commands and management APIs can reference consistently.

column3: I mapped Risk Classifier to Stage 3 > Software > In-situ monitoring & analytics because it evaluates command context and assigns runtime risk labels that support ongoing analysis and alert generation.
column4: Extend the custom HoneyPrint rule/context classifier and normalize selected equivalent commands across firmware dialects. (Python (re + dataclasses + enum))
column5: Assign consistent risk context to relevant firmware actions for alerting and analysis.
column6: Command risk labels with normalized intent, source dialect, and context passed to Stage 5 evidence handling.
